questions.request: Investigate process_file at /process/file in this Open WebUI revision. Trace the caller, the supplied file_id and the destination collection_name through authorization and the eventual processing or vector write. Explain whether the object authorized for input and the object affected by output are the same, and what happens for caller-owned versus another user's file. Do not assume the caller owns the destination collection. Identify visible conditions and specific remaining limits; this is behavior investigation.
questions.operation: process_file authorization, processing, and vector write

rules.claim: The POST /process/file handler first selects a file: admins use Files.get_file_by_id(form_data.file_id), while non-admin callers use Files.get_file_by_id_and_user_id(form_data.file_id, user.id). A missing selected file terminates with HTTP 404; a found file proceeds to content selection, metadata update, and either bypass or vector processing.
If the caller-scoped or admin file lookup yields no selected file, the handler raises HTTP 404 and does not reach processing or vector writing.
For a non-admin caller, the input file lookup is constrained by both the submitted file id and user.id; a matching row produces the selected file.
A non-null selected file permits the handler to continue into content loading and subsequent updates.

For the non-admin branch, get_file_by_id_and_user_id executes a database query filtered by both the supplied file id and the caller user id; it returns a validated file model for the first matching row and returns None when no matching row exists or an exception occurs.

observations.subject: POST /process/file
observations.claim: The endpoint obtains the caller from get_verified_user and an async database session. Admin callers use Files.get_file_by_id(file_id, db); non-admin callers use Files.get_file_by_id_and_user_id(file_id, user.id, db). A missing file raises HTTP 404 before processing.

observations.subject: caller
observations.claim: The handler's caller identity is the injected user object; the non-admin lookup passes user.id into the file query. The shown helper filters database rows by id=file_id and user_id=user.id, returning no file when there is no match or an exception occurs.

observations.subject: file_id
observations.claim: The request selects the file using form_data.file_id. For non-admin callers, the selected input object is restricted to a row matching both that id and the caller's user id. For admins, the shown endpoint calls an unscoped get_file_by_id helper, whose implementation was not read here.

observations.subject: file lookup
observations.claim: The decisive visible gate is whether the lookup returns a file. A non-admin request for another user's file produces no selected file through the shown user-scoped helper and therefore reaches the 404 branch; a caller-owned matching file can continue. Admin behavior is a separate role branch and is not restricted by the shown non-admin helper.

observations.subject: destination collection_name
observations.object: vector database collection and file metadata
observations.claim: After a file is selected, the handler derives collection_name from the request, defaulting to file-{file.id} only when the supplied value is None. It can update the file's content/status/hash and, when embedding is not bypassed, calls save_docs_to_vector_db with the selected docs and the supplied/derived collection_name. On a successful vector result it records that collection_name in the file metadata.

observations.subject: BYPASS_EMBEDDING_AND_RETRIEVAL and input mode
observations.claim: When BYPASS_EMBEDDING_AND_RETRIEVAL is true, the handler updates content/status/hash and returns without the shown vector save call. With form_data.content it deletes the file-{file.id} collection before constructing a document, while the later save call still receives the request/default collection_name. With an explicit collection_name and no content, it first queries file-{file.id} for existing content and otherwise uses file.data content; without content and without collection_name it loads from the file path or stored data.

behavior.explanation: For non-admin callers, input authorization is caller-scoped: the supplied file_id must identify a file whose database row also has user_id equal to the caller's user.id. A caller-owned matching file can proceed; another user's file is not selected by the shown helper and results in HTTP 404, so the processing/vector path is not reached. Admin callers take a distinct unscoped lookup branch in the endpoint, but the implementation and authorization behavior of get_file_by_id were not read. If a file is selected, the output target is the supplied collection_name, or file-{file.id} when collection_name is None. The source shown here does not establish that the caller owns, may write, or is otherwise authorized for that destination collection. Thus the input control object is the selected file, while the vector effect may target a separately supplied collection; they are not shown to be the same authorization object.

branches.condition: Non-admin caller and get_file_by_id_and_user_id(file_id, caller.user.id) returns a matching file
branches.explanation: The handler proceeds to one of the content, existing-collection, or file-loading branches. It then updates file data and either returns after the bypass path or attempts vector saving and final metadata updates.

branches.condition: Non-admin caller and the supplied file_id exists but its row has a different user_id
branches.explanation: The user-scoped query requires both id and user_id, so it returns no selected file for this caller. The endpoint raises HTTP 404 and does not reach processing or the shown vector-save call.

The endpoint calls get_file_by_id(file_id, db) rather than the shown caller-scoped helper, so the endpoint visibly takes an admin exception branch. The exact scope of that helper and any downstream destination authorization remain unread.

branches.condition: A file is selected and BYPASS_EMBEDDING_AND_RETRIEVAL is false
branches.explanation: The handler calls save_docs_to_vector_db with collection_name taken from the request or defaulted to file-{file.id}; on a truthy result it records the collection name on the selected file. No collection-owner or collection-access check is visible in the read endpoint window.

branches.condition: A file is selected and BYPASS_EMBEDDING_AND_RETRIEVAL is true
branches.explanation: The shown branch updates file content/status/hash and returns a successful response with collection_name set to None; it does not call the shown vector-save operation.
